info.name: GuestPilot Mobile API
info.description:
# GuestPilot Mobile API

Everything a mobile client needs, **in the order a client actually does it**. Run the folders top to bottom: later ones depend on ids the earlier ones save, and the collection is kept in an order where that works.

**This collection is run end to end by `npm run test:api`**, which is Postman's own runner (newman) against a freshly booted server with the mock POS and payment providers. 64 requests over all 62 routes, every one of them asserted. If a request here stops matching the API, that command fails — which is the point of it.

## Setup

1. Import `guestpilot-mobile.postman_environment.json` beside this file and select it.
2. Set `baseUrl` (default `http://localhost:3000`).
3. Run **1 · Discovery** first: it saves `branchId`, `itemId` and the modifier ids the cart requests need.
4. Run **2 · Account** in order, pasting the code from the email into `verificationCode` and the one from the SMS into `smsCode` when it asks.

Authentication is a Bearer token set on the collection, so every request inherits it. The few public endpoints override it to *No Auth* — those are the ones a client may call before anyone has signed in.

## The four codes you have to paste

`verificationCode`, `smsCode`, `otpCode` and `resetCode` arrive by email and SMS. Nothing in a collection can read them, so the request that needs one fails with a message saying exactly that. Paste and re-send. (`npm run test:api` reads them from the database instead, which is the one thing it does that a person does differently.)

## Six things that are not obvious from the endpoint list

1. **Registration does not sign you in.** `POST /auth/register` returns no token. The account must be verified first — the email's code and the SMS's — and `POST /auth/login` answers `401` until it is. `POST /auth/verify-email` is what returns the token pair.
2. **`branchId` is required on every cart write, and on every cart read and on the order** (`400` without it) — a basket is tied to one location, and is the account's own, the same one the website shows. It is still called `branchId` on the wire even though the rest of the system calls it a location. Omitting it answers `400` naming the field.
3. **Prices are never taken from the client.** Send a `price` on a cart item or a modifier and it is ignored — the server reads the offering and the item's own modifier data. `unitPrice` and `total` in the response are the real figures, and checkout re-reads them: a price that moved between the add and the order is refused rather than charged (ARCHITECTURE.md §4.7).
4. **The loyalty ceiling is a quote, not a balance.** `POST /loyalty/calculate-redemption` answers what the POS will let this guest redeem *against this cart* — with the campaign's own exchange rate applied and capped by the order total. Showing the wallet balance as the maximum invites a guest to ask for value the checkout then refuses.
5. **A POST answers `201`, not `200`** — Nest's default, including on routes whose Swagger said otherwise until 2026-09-23. The callbacks in folder 9 are the exception: a callback that is accepted answers `200`, because that is the only status the POS counts as delivered.
6. **Callbacks in folder 9 are not called by the app.** The payment gateway and the POS call them; they are here so you can see the shapes. The webhooks are expected to answer `401` from here, because an unsigned call is refused — that refusal is the assertion.

## Error shape

```json
{ "statusCode": 400, "message": ["branchId must be a string"], "timestamp": "...", "path": "/api/v1/cart/items" }
```

`message` is an **array of field constraints** for a validation failure, and a plain string for everything else. A `500` says only `Internal server error` by design.

## Three flows worth reading first

`FLOWS.md`, beside this file, walks the three parts of a client that are easiest to get wrong, with the same examples saved on the requests here:

1. **Options (modifiers)** — *1 · Discovery → Get one item*, then *5 · Cart → Add item with options*.
2. **Loyalty and wallet at checkout** — *6 → What can be redeemed against the cart*, then *7 → Place the order*.
3. **The referral programme** — *6 → Referral code* and *Referral stats*, then *2 · Account → Register* with `referralCode`.

Open a request and look at its **Examples**: each of these carries the success answer and the refusals a client must handle.

item.name: 1 · Discovery (no sign-in needed)
item.description:
What a client can show before anyone has an account. **Run “List locations” first** — it saves `branchId`, and every catalogue and cart call needs one.

A catalogue read that names no location is genuinely ambiguous when the estate has more than one, so these refuse rather than guessing which price list to serve.

request.description:
**Call this first, at launch — no token.** What this merchant’s instance offers, so the app draws only what exists instead of learning it from a `404`.

| Field | Use it to |
|---|---|
| `modules.loyalty` | show or hide loyalty: balances, free items, the counter card, **referrals** |
| `modules.wallet` | show or hide the wallet: its balance, top-up, history |
| `checkout.redemption` | show or hide the *amount to apply* at checkout — true when either module is on |
| `payment.providers` | the gateways to offer, in the operator’s order. One entry: offer no choice |
| `payment.default` | what an order with no `paymentProvider` is paid through |
| `payment.instant` | the gateways with **no payment page** — paid on choosing them. In development `mock-instant` is here; a real gateway never is |
| `payment.savedCards` | whether cards can be saved at all — hide the cards screen when false |
| `wallet.minTopUp`, `wallet.maxTopUp` | bounds for the top-up amount field, in currency |
| `currency` | the code to print beside every amount |
| `languages` | the languages content exists in, and the one to fall back to |

It is the instance’s, not a place’s: nothing here changes with `branchId`. A module can be switched off while the app is open, so a `404` from one of its routes still means *hide it* — read this again on the next launch or resume.

exec: pm.test('200 — with no token sent', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.eql(200));
const cfg = pm.response.json();
pm.test('names the merchant', () => { pm.expect(cfg.siteName).to.be.a('string').and.not.empty; });

pm.test('says which modules are on', () => { pm.expect(cfg.modules.loyalty).to.be.a('boolean'); pm.expect(cfg.modules.wallet).to.be.a('boolean'); pm.expect(cfg.checkout.redemption).to.eql(cfg.modules.loyalty || cfg.modules.wallet); });

pm.test('lists the gateways, the default being the first', () => { pm.expect(cfg.payment.providers).to.be.an('array').that.is.not.empty; pm.expect(cfg.payment.default).to.eql(cfg.payment.providers[0]); pm.expect(cfg.payment.instant).to.be.an('array'); pm.expect(cfg.payment.savedCards).to.be.a('boolean'); });

pm.test('carries the currency, the languages and the top-up range', () => { pm.expect(cfg.currency).to.be.a('string'); pm.expect(cfg.languages.supported).to.include(cfg.languages.default); pm.expect(cfg.wallet.minTopUp).to.be.below(cfg.wallet.maxTopUp); });
pm.test('says whether the merchant is taking orders', () => pm.expect(cfg.ordering.enabled).to.be.a('boolean'));

request.description:
Items with the price and availability **for this location**. `isAvailable: false` means the kitchen has stopped it — show it greyed rather than hiding it, and the cart will refuse to add it.

Each item is the same object *Get one item* answers, options included (`modifiersJson`, `optionNames`, `unavailableModifiers`) — a list screen already holds what the item screen needs. See *Get one item* for the fields.

exec: pm.test('200 — what is on sale here, at this location\u2019s prices', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.eql(200));
const xs = pm.response.json();
pm.test('the menu is not empty', () => pm.expect(xs.length).to.be.above(0));
// **A price is the location\u2019s, never the item\u2019s** — there is no `item.price`
// in this system, so a row without one is a catalogue defect rather than a
// free lunch.
pm.test('every item carries a price', () => xs.forEach((i) => pm.expect(i.price, i.internalName).to.be.above(0)));
// The plain item the cart requests below use: on sale, and choosable
// without choosing anything. Picked deterministically so two runs of one
// estate resolve to the same item.
const ordered = [...xs].sort((a, b) => String(a.slug || a.internalName).localeCompare(String(b.slug || b.internalName)) || String(a.id).localeCompare(String(b.id)));
const plain = ordered.find((i) => i.isAvailable !== false && (i.price || 0) > 0 && !(i.modifiersJson || []).length);
if (plain) { pm.environment.set('itemId', plain.id); }
// An item with exactly one group of options, for the add that chooses one.
const withOptions = ordered.find((i) => i.isAvailable !== false && (i.modifiersJson || []).length === 1 && ((i.modifiersJson[0].items || []).length > 0));
if (withOptions) {
pm.environment.set('optionItemId', withOptions.id);
pm.environment.set('modifierOptionId', withOptions.modifiersJson[0].items[0].id);
// **The shape an options screen is built from** (`FLOWS.md` §1): groups of
// options, each option an id, a name and a price the server decides.
pm.test('every item says which of its options are stopped here', () => xs.forEach((i) => pm.expect(i.unavailableModifiers, i.internalName).to.be.an('array')));
pm.test('every group of options has an id, a name and options with an id, a name and a price', () => xs.forEach((i) => (i.modifiersJson || []).forEach((g) => {
pm.expect(g.id, i.internalName).to.be.a('string');
pm.expect(g.name, i.internalName).to.be.a('string');
(g.items || []).forEach((o) => { pm.expect(o.id).to.be.a('string'); pm.expect(o.name).to.be.a('string'); pm.expect(o.price).to.be.a('number'); });
// **A named shape, never a database row** (ARCHITECTURE.md §7): these are all the fields there are.

pm.test('an item is exactly these fields', () => xs.forEach((x) => pm.expect(Object.keys(x).sort()).to.eql(["allergens", "category", "categoryId", "description", "galleryImages", "id", "imageUrl", "ingredients", "internalName", "isAvailable", "modifiersJson", "name", "nutritionalInfo", "optionNames", "price", "slug", "sortOrder", "tags", "unavailableModifiers"])));

pm.test('lists are lists, never null', () => xs.forEach((i) => ['galleryImages', 'tags', 'ingredients', 'allergens', 'modifiersJson'].forEach((k) => pm.expect(i[k], i.internalName + '.' + k).to.be.an('array'))));

request.description:
Full detail of one dish at one location: description, allergens, nutrition, pictures, and **its options**. The list routes return the same object per item.

**Options (`FLOWS.md` §1).** `modifiersJson` is a list of groups, `[]` when the dish has none:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| group `id`, `name` | the group; `name` is the POS’s own |
| group `restrictions.minQuantity` | how many options **must** be chosen — 0 or absent means optional |
| group `restrictions.maxQuantity` | how many **may** be chosen — 1 is a radio group; absent means no limit |
| group `items[]` | the options: `id`, `name`, `price` |
| option `price` | what choosing it adds to the dish, per unit |
| option `restrictions.defaultQuantity` | above 0: pre-select it |
| `optionNames` | translations, `{ "<group or option id>": { "hy": "…", "ru": "…" } }` — fall back to the `name` |
| `unavailableModifiers` | ids of options this location has run out of — show them disabled |

`isAvailable: false` is the whole dish stopped here: show it greyed, do not offer *Add*.

**Pictures.** `imageUrl` is the main image (the one every list shows) and `galleryImages` the further pictures for this screen only, in order, or null. Each is an absolute URL: an external store’s own, or the server’s MEDIA_BASE_URL (APP_BASE_URL when that is unset) followed by the stored path — never the host this request was sent to.

The saved examples leave out the fields that are not about options.

pm.test('a main image field and a gallery that is a list', () => { pm.expect(b).to.have.property('imageUrl'); pm.expect(b.galleryImages).to.be.an('array'); });
pm.test('the options this location has run out of, as a list', () => pm.expect(b.unavailableModifiers).to.be.an('array'));
// **A named shape, never a database row** (ARCHITECTURE.md §7): these are all the fields there are.

pm.test('an item is exactly these fields', () => pm.expect(Object.keys(b).sort()).to.eql(["allergens", "category", "categoryId", "description", "galleryImages", "id", "imageUrl", "ingredients", "internalName", "isAvailable", "modifiersJson", "name", "nutritionalInfo", "optionNames", "price", "slug", "sortOrder", "tags", "unavailableModifiers"]));

item.name: 2 · Account
item.description:
**In order.** Registration does not sign you in — the address must be verified first.

```
register  →  (code sent by email/SMS)  →  verify-email  →  tokens
```

A client that skips verification gets `401 Email not verified` from login. `verify-email` returns the same token pair login does, so a freshly verified guest is signed in already.

request.description:
`phone`, `email` and `password` are required; `name` and `referralCode` optional.

**Returns no token** — the response confirms a code was sent. Creates the guest in the POS at the same time, so the account exists on the merchant side immediately.

**`referralCode` — the only moment a referral can be recorded** (`FLOWS.md` §3). Send the inviter’s code (from *6 → Referral code*: their link `…/r/<code>`, or typed) and the inviter’s `registrations` goes up by one; the POS is told who referred the new guest and grants whatever the merchant’s programme gives. The answer is the same with or without one. **An unknown code is not an error**: the guest is registered without a referral and the answer does not say so — so check it first with *6 → Check a referral code*, which also names the inviter; case and spaces around a typed code do not matter. Keep it on the device from the moment the link is opened until this request is sent. Omit the field, or send `""`, when there is none.

Throttled to 10/minute. `409` means the phone or email is already registered.

`restaurantId` (optional) — the organisation (id or slug) the guest is signing up at: the one the app shows, or the `at` of the referral link they opened. A friend's referral is rewarded by its campaign. Default: the first organisation served.

exec: pm.test('201 — the account is made and a code is sent', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.eql(201));
pm.test('no token yet — the address is unverified', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().accessToken).to.be.undefined);

request.description:
**Two codes, and they differ** (P0-42): one by email, one by SMS. Set `verificationCode` (the email's) and `smsCode` (the SMS's) in the environment, then send. Each is checked on its own and kept: a right email code with a wrong SMS code answers `401 sms_code_invalid`; send again with the new `smsCode` and `"code": ""`.

**This returns the token pair** — a verified guest is signed in without a separate login.

item.description:
Every write needs `branchId` — the location the guest is ordering from. A cart belongs to one location; switching locations is an explicit call, not a field on each item.

**Prices are server-side.** Send `price` on an item or a modifier and it is ignored: the server reads the offering for that location and the item's own modifier data. The `unitPrice`, `modifierPrice` and `total` in the response are authoritative — render those, never your own sum.

**Options (modifiers), start to finish** — `FLOWS.md` §1.

```
GET  /menu/items/{id}?branchId=   →  modifiersJson (groups → items), optionNames, unavailableModifiers
POST /cart/items                  →  modifiers: [{ "id": "<option id>" }]   one entry per option chosen
                                  ←  the whole basket; each line carries modifiersJson, modifierPrice, unitPrice
```

`unitPrice` already includes `modifierPrice`. The same dish with the same options is one line whose quantity grows; a different choice is a second line.

item.name: 6 · Loyalty and wallet
item.description:
**The ceiling is quoted, not derived from a balance.** A balance says what a guest holds; the quote says what the POS will let them put towards *this* cart — with the campaign's exchange rate applied and capped by the order total. Offering the balance invites a guest to ask for value the checkout then refuses at the counter.

So: show the balance on the wallet screen, and the **quote** at checkout.

**Checkout, start to finish** — `FLOWS.md` §2.

```
POST /loyalty/calculate-redemption { branchId }   →  maxRedeemable, grantedDiscount, split
(guest types an amount ≤ maxRedeemable)
POST /orders { branchId, walletToSpend }           →  order.walletSpent, order.discount, order.totalToCharge + a payment target
```

`walletToSpend` is the one amount for **every** balance, points included. `loyaltyPointsToSpend` is never sent.

**Referrals** — `FLOWS.md` §3. *Referral code* gives the guest a code, a link and a QR; a friend joins by sending that code as `referralCode` to *2 · Account → Register*, and at no other moment. The reward, if the merchant has set one up, is the POS’s and shows up as a balance or a free item — this API never returns one.

item.name: What can be redeemed against the cart

request.description:
**Call this on the checkout screen, and again whenever the basket changes** (`FLOWS.md` §2). It reads the guest’s basket **at `branchId`** (required) and asks the POS what the guest may put towards it. No items and no total are sent.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `available` | false: nothing can be applied — hide the control |
| `maxRedeemable` | the most the guest may apply, **in currency** — the upper bound of the one *amount to apply* input |
| `grantedDiscount` | what the POS takes off whatever the guest does (a free item earned) — subtract it from the total shown |
| `split` | where an amount lands, in the POS’s order — for display |

**One input, not one per programme.** `split` is a cascade: each row’s `cap` assumes the rows before it were filled. To show what a typed amount will come to, walk the rows in order: take the smaller of `cap` and what is left; when `step` is above 1 round that down to a multiple of `step` (one item’s price — a balance of free items pays for whole items); when `step` is 0 take all of `cap` or nothing. The sum is what the order will apply, which can be less than typed. `walletIds` join to `wallets[].id` from *Loyalty balance* for the programme’s name.

Then send the amount as `walletToSpend` to *Place the order*.

A basket that is empty or at another location, and a guest with nothing to spend, all answer `{ available: false, maxRedeemable: 0, grantedDiscount: 0, split: [] }`. `404` means both the loyalty and the wallet module are off.

// **A quote, not a balance.** It is what this guest may put towards *this*
// cart, with the campaign\u2019s own rate applied and capped by the total.
pm.test('the split is rows of cap, step and wallet ids, summing to no more than the ceiling', () => {
const body = pm.response.json();
pm.expect(body.split).to.be.an('array');
body.split.forEach((row) => {
pm.expect(row.cap).to.be.above(0);
pm.expect(row.step).to.be.at.least(0);
pm.expect(row.walletIds).to.be.an('array');
pm.expect(body.split.reduce((sum, row) => sum + row.cap, 0)).to.be.at.most(body.maxRedeemable);

pm.test('available says whether there is anything to apply', () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.available).to.eql(body.maxRedeemable > 0); pm.expect(body.grantedDiscount).to.be.at.least(0); });

This guest’s referral code, link and QR (`FLOWS.md` §3). No body. **The same code on every call** — the first makes it — so call it when the invite screen opens.

- `code` — eight characters, `A–Z` and `2–9` without `0 O 1 I`.
- `link` — what to hand to the share sheet. It opens the merchant’s website registration with the code attached; register `/r/*` as a universal/app link to open the app instead, and read the last path segment as the code.
- `qrDataUrl` — a PNG of the link, as a data URI.

**How a friend uses it:** as `referralCode` when their account is created — on *2 · Account → Register*, or on *3 → Verify the code* when that sign-in creates the account. Nothing attaches a referrer to an account that already exists. Their app can first ask *Check a referral code* whose it is, and reports the link being opened with *Count a referral link opened in the app*.

**No reward comes back from this API.** Whether a referral earns anything is the merchant’s POS programme; it shows up as a balance or a free item. `404` when the loyalty module is off.

`link` ends `?at=<organisation>` — where it is shared from; add `?restaurantId=` here to name it, as on the loyalty reads. A friend who follows it is registered there.

item.description:
Placing an order is asynchronous and involves a payment gateway.

```
POST /orders  →  payment form/URL  →  guest pays  →  gateway calls back  →  order reaches the till
```

**The response to `POST /orders` is not a completed order.** Send the guest to the payment target it returns and poll the status endpoint, or wait for a push. Never treat a `201` as paid.

**What the order answers** — `itemsTotal`, `discount` (what the POS’s campaigns took off), `walletSpent` (what was actually applied from the guest’s balances) and `totalToCharge = itemsTotal − discount − walletSpent`. **No `paymentFormUrl` and no `paymentForm` means `totalToCharge` was 0** and the order is already placed.

**Paying in development.** Two test gateways stand in for a real one. `mock-instant` is paid on choosing it — *Place and pay — instant test gateway* — so an app needs no web view to get an order placed. `mock` has a page with *Pay* and *Decline*, and is what the rest of this folder uses to show an order that is still awaiting payment. A real gateway behaves like `mock`: it answers something to open.

request.description:
Builds the order from the guest’s basket **at `branchId`** (required) — **no items in the body**, options included as the basket holds them. An empty basket, or one at another location, answers `400 Cart is empty`.

**`walletToSpend` is the one amount to apply from the guest’s balances — every kind, points included** (`FLOWS.md` §2). Take it from the guest, bounded by `maxRedeemable` from *6 → What can be redeemed against the cart*. The name is historical. `0` or omitted applies nothing.

**Asking for more than the POS will cover is not an error**: the order applies what it can. So read the answer rather than assuming:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `order.itemsTotal` | the basket, options included |
| `order.discount` | what the POS’s campaigns took off (the quote’s `grantedDiscount`) |
| `order.walletSpent` | what was **actually applied** from the balances |
| `order.totalToCharge` | `itemsTotal − discount − walletSpent` — what the card is charged |

**Then pay.** `paymentFormUrl` → open it in a web view (a path with no host is relative to this API). `paymentForm: { action, fields }` instead → the gateway is reached by a form POST. **Neither → `totalToCharge` was 0 and the order is already placed.** A `201` is not a paid order: poll the status endpoint or wait for a push.

**Never send `loyaltyPointsToSpend`.** Any value above 0 is refused — see the example. It stays in the schema only so an old client is told why.

**A second order for the same basket replaces the first** while that one is unpaid.

**Other optional fields, omitted here on purpose:** `paymentProvider` (a gateway name — leave it out for the default) and `scheduledAt` (an **ISO 8601** timestamp for a pre-order). Sending `""` for either is a validation error, not a default.

If a price moved or an option ran out since the basket was filled, the answer is `400` with the sentence to show; the basket has been corrected, so reload it and let the guest order again.

**In development, to skip the payment page entirely**, see *Place and pay — instant test gateway* above.

const order = b.order || b;
pm.test('an order number to pay against', () => pm.expect(order.orderNumber).to.be.a('string'));
// **A 201 is not a paid order.** It is payment_pending until the gateway
// confirms, which is what folder 9 stands in for.
pm.test('not paid yet', () => pm.expect(order.paymentStatus).to.eql('pending'));
pm.test('charged what the cart came to', () => pm.expect(order.itemsTotal).to.be.above(0));
